follow-up time: Not specified, but included follow-ups regarding recovery and breastfeeding
outcome: Presence of SARS-CoV-2 in breast milk, vaginal secretions, cord blood, and neonatal serum
Presence of IgM and IgG antibodies to SARS-CoV-2 in breast milk, cord blood, and neonatal serum
cohort: Fourteen pregnant women with laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 who delivered during hospitalization at a tertiary-care center in Wuhan, China, and their infants
finding: The study suggests that breastfeeding has a low risk of transmitting SARS-CoV-2 and that infants may acquire passive immunity through antibodies present in breast milk.
